summary: A 1939 CT-2 wood fire lookout on the Coconino National Forest, one of few of its design left. HistoriCorps Phase I work is listed; rental and staffing are unconfirmed.

facts.design: 30-ft wood CT-2 tower with an R-3 modified L-4 14 x 14 ft live-in cab and catwalk

events.note: CT-2 wood tower. The register and federal record point to 1939; Wikipedia gives 1933 or 1939
Listing date conflicts: Wikipedia says December 14, 1987; the federal record shows a January 28, 1988 publication date
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, April 1, 2001

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia gives 1933 or 1939. The register and the federal record point to 1939, which the story follows.

Wikipedia places the tower in the Coronado National Forest; the register and federal record say Coconino. The register's own cooperator line names the Mogollon Rim Ranger District while its description names Long Valley, so the district is not settled.

notes_for_editor: Build year 1939 agrees across the register and the federal record; Wikipedia's 1933 alternative is noted. Listing date for the NRHP is unsettled (Wikipedia Dec 14, 1987 vs federal record Jan 28, 1988). Rental and staffing status are NOT confirmed. The Arizona Daily Sun article on HistoriCorps restoring the tower to become a rentable cabin returned HTTP 429 on repeated tries and was not read, so no claim rests on it; it is worth a re-read. The Living New Deal page returned 403. The NRHP nomination PDFs on NPGallery are scanned, with no text layer. The Coconino NF cabin pages I read (camping-cabins and Rooms With a View) do not mention Buck Mountain. HistoriCorps Phase I has no date in the sources read. Access and visit are omitted for lack of a source. No corrections proposed; brief's 1939 build is supported.
